verdicts.note: Impaired fecundity trends, US NSFG. Wall 4 by topic, but it sizes the population ART could in principle serve.
OB/GYN residents' attitudes to discussing age decline and oocyte cryopreservation — the clinical supply side of the belief channel.
Varicocele repair and ART outcomes.
Relative contribution of ART versus OVULATION INDUCTION to US multiple births after the SART embryo-limit guidance. Third record in the frame separating the OI channel — A.12 should have all of them.
Political economy of expertise in fertility governance.
No abstract, no venue, 1986 chapter.
Reply letter on ovarian reserve screening.
No abstract. US childlessness cohort analysis.
Traffic noise and air pollution against infertility risk, Danish cohort. B.2/B.6's.
Why women delay. A.15's, though it bears on whether delay is chosen or constrained.
Incidence of medical CONSULTATION for fecundity problems in France, with competing risks. The entry step into treatment, in a universal-coverage setting.
Educational homogamy in Ireland.
Maternal age at birth and daughters' childlessness. A.19's.
Religion and childlessness among Austrian researchers.
**Celebrity magazines MISREPRESENT fertility at advanced ages.** P6's belief channel has a documented supply side: this is where the overestimate of ART's power comes from, not just that it exists.
CHINA's prospective ART insurance coverage. A very large access expansion in a very-low-fertility setting — the highest-stakes P1 exposure in the frame if it has been evaluated.
Provider competence for transgender fertility care.
Hungarian insurance claims cost of female infertility.
**TIME TO BIRTH FOR SPONTANEOUS AND ART BIRTHS AMONG INFERTILE GROUPS.** Compares treated and untreated infertile people — the comparison arm 1's counterfactual requires and almost never has.
No abstract. The desired-versus-actual family size gap and 'practical options' — the clinical framing of arm 1's promise.
Human capital and birth timing, Germany.
Sequence analysis of Danish family formation.
Overview of European fertility.
Reproductive ageing and ELECTIVE preservation, review.
Cycle length and ovarian reserve biomarkers.
Iranian study of delay factors.

**BJOG systematic review of PLANNED oocyte cryopreservation: cost-efficiency AND UTILISATION.** Utilisation is the number P5 most needs — how many women who freeze eggs ever return to use them decides whether the technology produces births at all.

**A MUNICIPALLY FUNDED oocyte cryopreservation programme in Japan, with outcomes.** A publicly funded elective-preservation programme is P5's exposure and PI call 2's cell in its strongest available form — a real subsidy, a defined population, reported early outcomes. Priority.
Postpartum psychosis after IVF.
Liquidity constraints and health-care demand. The general form of arm 2's price mechanism, reached by citation.
Commentary on infertility disparities and access.

**The ONTARIO FERTILITY PROGRAM — 5,000 publicly funded IVF cycles a year, introduced as a discrete policy.** A clean non-US access expansion with a before/after design. The outcome here is duplicate consultations, so full text must say whether births were followed.
COVID and Spanish birth registers. A shock to births generally, not to ART access.

**'THE LIMITS TO FERTILITY RECUPERATION.'** Titled on the ceiling of A.17's claim: how much of postponed fertility gets recovered at all, by any route. The denominator against which ART's contribution has to be judged.
Qualitative: midlife intending mothers' expectations of ART. Belief side, but in the population that acts on it.
How patients and physicians define infertility.

**A SHADOW RECORD: 'Faculty Opinions recommendation of Reproductive aging and elective fertility preservation.'** It carries the recommended paper's abstract verbatim, which is exactly why the shadow gate exists. Not a work; the target is W2886163022 in this same batch.
Chinese students' fertility awareness, scale development.
The International Glossary on Infertility and Fertility Care — definitions. Useful for harmonising terms at extraction; not evidence.
No abstract. Determinants of IVF treatment outcome.
ICMART world report 2005 — the global series, earlier edition than the anchored glossary.
Environmental factors in declining fertility. B.2/B.6's.
ESHRE EIM, 2009 edition.
Infertility prevalence in sub-Saharan Africa. Wall 4 and Wall 8 both.
No abstract. Birth outcomes in infertile couples with and without ART.
ASRM practice-committee opinion on multiple gestation from infertility therapy.
CDC ART Surveillance 2016 — the US series, later edition than the 2013 anchor.
Synthetic control methodology for population health interventions. A methods record, and a usable one if the chapter ends up wanting a design for a single-country ART policy change.
Delayed childbearing effects on fertility and pregnancy outcome.
Sweden's embryo-transfer reduction against DELIVERY and multiple-birth rates. The delivery-rate half is A.17's quantity — flag as both_arms_present at full text.
**'A PERSISTENT MISPERCEPTION: ART CAN REVERSE THE AGED BIOLOGICAL CLOCK.'** P6's mechanism named in a title, in Fertility and Sterility. The chapter's P6 section should open on this.
No abstract. Student perceptions of ART 'in the era of oocyte freezing'.
No abstract. Access barriers for male-factor infertility.
Britain: whether higher-educated women RECUPERATE births at older ages. The observed recuperation rate — what actually happens without attributing it to treatment.
Historiography of voluntary-childlessness scholarship.
Welfare reform and teenage childbearing. Reached by design similarity.
How infertility definitions change measured prevalence. Methodological, and it matters for Wall 4's boundary.
Practice guidance on responding to infertility.

**'RUNNING OUT OF TIME?' — the biological clock's effect on the DYNAMICS of fertility intentions AND union formation.** Belief and behaviour in one design, on panel data. Among the strongest P6 candidates found.
Fertility and longevity.
